title_en: Regulations on the Implementation of the Tendering and Bidding Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Tendering and Bidding Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Tendering and Bidding Law) for the purpose of regulating tendering and bidding activities.

Article 2 The term "construction projects" as mentioned in Article 3 of the Tendering and Bidding Law shall refer to projects and goods and services related to project construction.
The term "projects" as mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall refer to construction projects, including the construction, reconstruction, and expansion of buildings and structures, as well as their related decoration, demolition, and repair, etc.; the term "goods related to project construction" shall refer to equipment, materials, etc., which constitute an inseparable component of the project and are necessary for realizing the basic functions of the project; the term "services related to project construction" shall refer to surveying, design, supervision, and other services required for completing the project.

Article 3 The specific scope and scale standards of construction projects that must undergo tendering according to law shall be formulated by the development and reform department of the State Council jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council, and shall be published and implemented after being submitted to the State Council for approval.

Article 4 The development and reform department of the State Council shall guide and coordinate the national tendering and bidding work, and shall exercise supervision and inspection over the tendering and bidding activities of major national construction projects. The departments of industry and information technology, housing and urban-rural construction, transport, railway, water resources, commerce, etc., of the State Council shall, in accordance with the division of their respective duties as prescribed, exercise supervision over the relevant tendering and bidding activities.
The development and reform departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall guide and coordinate the tendering and bidding work within their respective administrative regions. The relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the division of their respective duties as prescribed, exercise supervision over tendering and bidding activities, and shall investigate and deal with illegal acts in tendering and bidding activities according to law. Where a local people's government at or above the county level has otherwise provided for the division of supervisory duties of its subordinate departments concerning tendering and bidding activities, such provisions shall prevail.
The financial departments shall, according to law, exercise supervision over the implementation of the government procurement policies in government procurement construction projects that adopt tendering and bidding.
The supervisory organs shall, according to law, exercise supervision over the persons subject to supervision in relation to tendering and bidding activities.

Article 5 Local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts may, in light of actual needs, establish unified and standardized tendering and bidding trading venues to provide services for tendering and bidding activities. The tendering and bidding trading venues shall not have a subordinate relationship with administrative supervision departments, and shall not be operated for profit.
The State encourages the use of information networks for electronic tendering and bidding.
Article 6 State functionaries are prohibited from illegally interfering in tendering and bidding activities in any manner.

Article 7 For a project that must undergo tendering according to law and for which the procedures for project approval or verification need to be fulfilled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, the scope of tendering, the method of tendering, and the organizational form of tendering shall be submitted to the project approval or verification department for approval or verification. The project approval or verification department shall promptly notify the relevant administrative supervision departments of the scope of tendering, the method of tendering, and the organizational form of tendering as determined upon approval or verification.

Article 8 For a project that must undergo tendering according to law and in which state-owned funds hold a controlling or dominant position, open tendering shall be adopted; however, under any of the following circumstances, invited tendering may be adopted:
(1) The technology is complex, there are special requirements, or the project is subject to natural environmental constraints, leaving only a small number of potential bidders to choose from;
(2) The cost of adopting open tendering accounts for an excessively large proportion of the contract amount of the project.
Where the circumstance specified in subparagraph (2) of the preceding paragraph exists in a project falling under the provisions of Article 7 of these Regulations, the project approval or verification department shall make a determination when approving or verifying the project; for other projects, the tenderer shall apply to the relevant administrative supervision department for a determination.

Article 10 The term "a tenderer having the capability to prepare tender documents and to organize bid evaluation" as mentioned in paragraph 2 of Article 12 of the Tendering and Bidding Law shall mean that the tenderer has technical, economic, and other professional personnel commensurate with the scale and complexity of the tendering project.

Article 11 The departments of housing and urban-rural construction, commerce, development and reform, industry and information technology, etc., of the State Council shall, in accordance with the division of their respective duties as prescribed, exercise supervision and administration over tendering agencies according to law.
Article 12 A tendering agency shall have a certain number of professional personnel with the corresponding capability to prepare tender documents, organize bid evaluation, etc.

Article 13 A tendering agency shall carry out its tendering agency business within the scope entrusted by the tenderer, and no unit or individual shall illegally interfere.
When acting as an agent for tendering business, a tendering agency shall comply with the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations concerning tenderers. A tendering agency shall not bid or act as an agent for bidding in the tendering project for which it acts as an agent, nor shall it provide consulting services to bidders of the tendering project for which it acts as an agent.

Article 14 A tenderer shall enter into a written entrustment contract with the appointed tendering agency, and the fee rates agreed upon in the contract shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 15 For an open tendering project, a tender announcement shall be published and tender documents shall be prepared in accordance with the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations.
Where a tenderer adopts a pre-qualification method to examine the qualifications of potential bidders, it shall publish a pre-qualification announcement and prepare pre-qualification documents.
The pre-qualification announcement and tender announcement for a project that must undergo tendering according to law shall be published on the media designated by the development and reform department of the State Council according to law. The contents of the pre-qualification announcement or tender announcement for the same tendering project published on different media shall be consistent. No fees shall be charged for the publication of domestic pre-qualification announcements and tender announcements for projects that must undergo tendering according to law on the designated media.
The preparation of pre-qualification documents and tender documents for a project that must undergo tendering according to law shall use the standard texts formulated by the development and reform department of the State Council jointly with the relevant administrative supervision departments.

Article 16 A tenderer shall sell the pre-qualification documents or tender documents at the time and place specified in the pre-qualification announcement, tender announcement, or invitation to bid. The selling period for pre-qualification documents or tender documents shall not be less than 5 days.
The fees charged by a tenderer for selling pre-qualification documents or tender documents shall be limited to covering the costs of printing and postage, and shall not be for profit.

Article 17 A tenderer shall reasonably determine the time for submitting pre-qualification application documents. For a project that must undergo tendering according to law, the time for submitting pre-qualification application documents shall not be less than 5 days from the date on which the sale of pre-qualification documents ceases.

Article 18 Pre-qualification shall be conducted in accordance with the standards and methods specified in the pre-qualification documents.
For a project that must undergo tendering according to law and in which state-owned funds hold a controlling or dominant position, the tenderer shall establish a qualification examination committee to examine the pre-qualification application documents. The qualification examination committee and its members shall comply with the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations concerning the bid evaluation committee and its members.

Article 19 After the completion of pre-qualification, the tenderer shall promptly issue a pre-qualification result notice to the pre-qualification applicants. Applicants that fail to pass the pre-qualification shall not have the qualification to bid.
If the number of applicants that pass the pre-qualification is less than 3, tendering shall be conducted anew.

Article 20 Where a tenderer adopts a post-qualification method to examine the qualifications of bidders, the bid evaluation committee shall, after the bid opening, examine the qualifications of bidders in accordance with the standards and methods specified in the tender documents.

Article 21 A tenderer may make necessary clarifications or modifications to the pre-qualification documents or tender documents already issued. Where the content of the clarifications or modifications may affect the preparation of pre-qualification application documents or bid documents, the tenderer shall notify in writing all potential bidders that have obtained the pre-qualification documents or tender documents at least 3 days before the deadline for submission of pre-qualification application documents, or at least 15 days before the deadline for submission of bids; if the remaining time is less than 3 days or 15 days, the tenderer shall extend the deadline for submission of pre-qualification application documents or bid documents accordingly.

Article 22 Where a potential bidder or any other interested party has any objection to the pre-qualification documents, it shall raise it 2 days before the deadline for submission of pre-qualification application documents; where it has any objection to the tender documents, it shall raise it 10 days before the deadline for submission of bids. The tenderer shall make a reply within 3 days from the date of receipt of the objection; before making the reply, it shall suspend the tendering and bidding activities.

Article 23 Where the contents of the pre-qualification documents or tender documents prepared by a tenderer violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, violate the principles of openness, fairness, impartiality, and good faith, and affect the results of pre-qualification or the bidding by potential bidders, the tenderer of a project that must undergo tendering according to law shall, after revising the pre-qualification documents or tender documents, conduct tendering anew.

Article 24 Where a tenderer divides a tendering project into bid lots, it shall comply with the relevant provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law, and shall not use the division of bid lots to restrict or exclude potential bidders. A tenderer of a project that must undergo tendering according to law shall not use the division of bid lots to evade tendering.
Article 25 A tenderer shall specify the bid validity period in the tender documents. The bid validity period shall be calculated from the deadline for submission of bid documents.

Article 26 Where a tenderer requires bidders to submit a bid bond in the tender documents, the bid bond shall not exceed 2% of the estimated price of the tendering project. The validity period of the bid bond shall be consistent with the bid validity period.
For a domestic bidding unit in a project that must undergo tendering according to law, the bid bond submitted in cash or by check shall be transferred from its basic account.
A tenderer shall not misappropriate bid bonds.

Article 27 A tenderer may decide on its own whether to prepare a base price. A tendering project may have only one base price. The base price must be kept confidential.
An intermediary institution that accepts the entrustment to prepare a base price shall not participate in the bidding of the project for which it prepares the base price, nor shall it prepare bid documents or provide consulting services for the bidders of such project.
Where a tenderer sets a maximum bid price, it shall specify the maximum bid price or the method for calculating the maximum bid price in the tender documents. A tenderer shall not set a minimum bid price.
Article 28 A tenderer shall not organize site visits for individual or some potential bidders.

Article 29 A tenderer may, according to law, conduct a general contracting tender for all or part of the project and the goods and services related to project construction. Where the projects, goods, and services included in the general contracting scope in the form of provisional sum prices fall within the scope of projects that must undergo tendering according to law and meet the scale standards prescribed by the State, they shall undergo tendering according to law.
The term "provisional sum price" as mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall refer to the amount of the project, goods, or services that cannot be determined at the time of the general contracting tender and is tentatively estimated by the tenderer in the tender documents.

Article 30 For a project with complex technology or where the technical specifications cannot be precisely formulated, the tenderer may conduct the tendering in two stages.
In the first stage, bidders shall submit technical proposals without prices in accordance with the requirements of the tender announcement or invitation to bid, and the tenderer shall determine the technical standards and requirements and prepare the tender documents based on the technical proposals submitted by the bidders.
In the second stage, the tenderer shall provide the tender documents to the bidders that submitted technical proposals in the first stage, and the bidders shall submit bid documents including the final technical scheme and bid price in accordance with the requirements of the tender documents.
If the tenderer requires bidders to submit a bid bond, it shall make such requirement in the second stage.

Article 31 Where a tenderer terminates the tendering, it shall promptly publish an announcement or notify in writing the invited potential bidders or those that have already obtained the pre-qualification documents or tender documents. If pre-qualification documents or tender documents have been sold or bid bonds have been collected, the tenderer shall promptly refund the fees collected for the pre-qualification documents or tender documents, as well as the bid bonds collected together with the bank deposit interest for the corresponding period.

Article 33 Bidders participating in the bidding of a project that must undergo tendering according to law shall not be subject to regional or departmental restrictions, and no unit or individual shall illegally interfere.

Article 34 A legal person, other organization, or individual that has an interest relationship with the tenderer that may affect the impartiality of the tendering shall not participate in the bidding.
Different units whose persons in charge are the same person or which have a controlling or management relationship between them shall not bid for the same bid lot or the same tendering project that is not divided into bid lots.
Where the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs are violated, the relevant bids shall all be invalid.

Article 35 Where a bidder withdraws a bid document already submitted, it shall notify the tenderer in writing before the deadline for submission of bids. If the tenderer has collected a bid bond, it shall refund it within 5 days from the date of receipt of the written notice of withdrawal from the bidder.
Where a bidder revokes its bid document after the bid deadline, the tenderer may refuse to refund the bid bond.

Article 36 The tenderer shall reject bid documents submitted by applicants that have not passed the pre-qualification, as well as bid documents that are delivered late or not sealed in accordance with the requirements of the tender documents.
The tenderer shall truthfully record the time of delivery and the sealing status of the bid documents, and shall keep them on file for future reference.

Article 37 A tenderer shall specify in the pre-qualification announcement, tender announcement, or invitation to bid whether it accepts bids from joint ventures.
Where a tenderer accepts bids from a joint venture and conducts pre-qualification, the joint venture shall be formed before the submission of pre-qualification application documents. If the joint venture adds, removes, or replaces members after pre-qualification, its bid shall be invalid.
Where any party to a joint venture bids individually in its own name or participates in another joint venture's bid in the same tendering project, all relevant bids shall be invalid.

Article 38 Where a bidder undergoes a major change such as merger, division, or bankruptcy, it shall promptly notify the tenderer in writing. If the bidder no longer meets the qualification conditions specified in the pre-qualification documents or tender documents, or its bid affects the impartiality of the tendering, its bid shall be invalid.
Article 43 Applicants submitting pre-qualification application documents shall comply with the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations concerning bidders.

Article 44 A tenderer shall open bids at the time and place specified in the tender documents.
If there are fewer than 3 bidders, the bids shall not be opened; the tenderer shall conduct tendering anew.
If a bidder has any objection to the bid opening, it shall raise it at the bid opening site, and the tenderer shall make a reply on the spot and keep a record.

Article 45 The State shall implement unified professional classification standards and management measures for bid evaluation experts. The specific standards and measures shall be formulated by the development and reform department of the State Council jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, as well as the relevant departments of the State Council, shall establish comprehensive bid evaluation expert databases.

Article 46 Except for special tendering projects as specified in paragraph 3 of Article 37 of the Tendering and Bidding Law, for projects that must undergo tendering according to law, the expert members of the bid evaluation committee shall be determined by random selection from the list of experts in relevant specialties in the bid evaluation expert database. No unit or individual may designate or indirectly designate expert members to participate in the bid evaluation committee by any means such as explicit or implicit suggestion.
A tenderer of a project that must undergo tendering according to law shall not replace the members of the bid evaluation committee determined according to law except for the reasons specified in the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations. The replacement of expert members of the bid evaluation committee shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
Members of the bid evaluation committee who have an interest relationship with a bidder shall voluntarily withdraw.
The relevant administrative supervision departments shall, in accordance with the division of their respective duties as prescribed, supervise the method of determining the members of the bid evaluation committee, the selection of bid evaluation experts, and the bid evaluation activities. Staff members of an administrative supervision department shall not serve as members of the bid evaluation committee for projects under the supervision of that department.

Article 47 The term "special tendering projects" as mentioned in paragraph 3 of Article 37 of the Tendering and Bidding Law shall refer to projects where the technology is complex, the specialty is strong, or the State has special requirements, and where experts determined by random selection may not be competent for the bid evaluation work.

Article 48 A tenderer shall provide the bid evaluation committee with the information necessary for bid evaluation, but shall not explicitly or implicitly suggest its preference for or exclusion of specific bidders.
The tenderer shall reasonably determine the bid evaluation time based on factors such as the scale and technical complexity of the project. If more than one-third of the members of the bid evaluation committee consider the bid evaluation time insufficient, the tenderer shall appropriately extend it.
During the bid evaluation process, if a member of the bid evaluation committee has a ground for withdrawal, leaves without permission, or is unable to continue the bid evaluation due to health or other reasons, such member shall be promptly replaced. The evaluation conclusions made by the replaced member of the bid evaluation committee shall be invalid, and the replacement member shall conduct the evaluation anew.

Article 49 Members of the bid evaluation committee shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations, and in accordance with the bid evaluation standards and methods specified in the tender documents, objectively and impartially evaluate the bid documents. The bid evaluation standards and methods not specified in the tender documents shall not be used as the basis for bid evaluation.
Members of the bid evaluation committee shall not have private contact with bidders, shall not accept property or other benefits given by bidders, shall not solicit the tenderer's intention regarding the determination of the winning bidder, shall not accept any requirements explicitly or implicitly raised by any unit or individual to favor or exclude specific bidders, and shall not engage in any other acts that are not objective or impartial in the performance of their duties.

Article 50 If a tendering project has a base price, the tenderer shall announce it at the time of bid opening. The base price may only be used as a reference for bid evaluation, and the closeness of the bid price to the base price shall not be used as a condition for winning the bid, nor shall the bid price exceeding the range of deviation above or below the base price be used as a condition for rejecting a bid.

Article 52 Where the bid documents contain unclear meanings, obvious textual or calculation errors, and the bid evaluation committee considers that the bidder needs to make necessary clarifications or explanations, it shall notify the bidder in writing. The clarifications or explanations made by the bidder shall be in written form and shall not go beyond the scope of the bid documents or change the substantive content of the bid documents.
The bid evaluation committee shall not suggest or induce bidders to make clarifications or explanations, and shall not accept clarifications or explanations proactively offered by bidders.

Article 53 After the completion of bid evaluation, the bid evaluation committee shall submit a written bid evaluation report and a list of candidates for winning the bid to the tenderer. The number of candidates for winning the bid shall not exceed 3, and they shall be ranked.
The bid evaluation report shall be signed by all members of the bid evaluation committee. A member of the bid evaluation committee who has a dissenting opinion on the bid evaluation results shall explain the dissenting opinion and reasons in writing, and the bid evaluation report shall note such dissenting opinion. If a member of the bid evaluation committee refuses to sign the bid evaluation report and fails to explain the dissenting opinion and reasons in writing, such member shall be deemed to have agreed to the bid evaluation results.

Article 54 For a project that must undergo tendering according to law, the tenderer shall publicize the candidates for winning the bid within 3 days from the date of receipt of the bid evaluation report, and the publicity period shall not be less than 3 days.
If a bidder or any other interested party has any objection to the bid evaluation results of a project that must undergo tendering according to law, it shall raise it during the publicity period of the candidates for winning the bid. The tenderer shall make a reply within 3 days from the date of receipt of the objection; before making the reply, it shall suspend the tendering and bidding activities.

Article 55 For a project that must undergo tendering according to law and in which state-owned funds hold a controlling or dominant position, the tenderer shall determine the candidate for winning the bid ranked first as the winning bidder. If the candidate ranked first gives up winning the bid, is unable to perform the contract due to force majeure, fails to submit a performance bond in accordance with the requirements of the tender documents, or is found to have engaged in illegal acts affecting the bid result, or any other circumstance that makes the candidate ineligible for winning the bid, the tenderer may, in the order of the list of candidates for winning the bid proposed by the bid evaluation committee, determine other candidates as the winning bidder successively, or may conduct tendering anew.

Article 56 If a candidate for winning the bid undergoes significant changes in its business or financial conditions, or has illegal acts, and the tenderer considers that such circumstances may affect its performance capability, the original bid evaluation committee shall, before issuing the letter of acceptance, review and confirm the matter in accordance with the standards and methods specified in the tender documents.

Article 57 The tenderer and the winning bidder shall sign a written contract in accordance with the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations, and the main terms of the contract, such as the subject matter, price, quality, and performance period, shall be consistent with the contents of the tender documents and the winning bidder's bid document. The tenderer and the winning bidder shall not conclude any other agreement that deviates from the substantive content of the contract.
The tenderer shall, within 5 days after the signing of the written contract at the latest, refund the bid bonds together with the bank deposit interest for the corresponding period to the winning bidder and the unsuccessful bidders.

Article 58 If the tender documents require the winning bidder to submit a performance bond, the winning bidder shall submit it in accordance with the requirements of the tender documents. The performance bond shall not exceed 10% of the amount of the contract for the winning bid.

Article 59 The winning bidder shall perform its obligations in accordance with the contract and complete the project for which the bid was won. The winning bidder shall not assign the project for which the bid was won to others, nor shall it divide the project into parts and assign them separately to others.
The winning bidder may, in accordance with the contract or with the consent of the tenderer, subcontract part of the non-main, non-critical work of the project for which the bid was won to others for completion. The subcontractor shall have the corresponding qualification conditions and shall not sub-subcontract.
The winning bidder shall be responsible to the tenderer for the subcontracted work, and the subcontractor shall bear joint and several liability for the subcontracted work.

Article 60 If a bidder or any other interested party considers that a tendering and bidding activity does not comply with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, it may file a complaint with the relevant administrative supervision department within 10 days from the date on which it knows or should have known of the matter. The complaint shall contain clear requests and necessary supporting materials.
Where a complaint is filed concerning the matters specified in Articles 22, 44, and 54 of these Regulations, an objection shall first be raised with the tenderer, and the period for replying to the objection shall not be counted within the period specified in the preceding paragraph.

Article 61 If a complainant files a complaint with two or more administrative supervision departments that have the authority to accept the complaint regarding the same matter, the administrative supervision department that first receives the complaint shall be responsible for handling it.
The administrative supervision department shall decide whether to accept the complaint within 3 working days from the date of receipt of the complaint, and shall make a written handling decision within 30 working days from the date of acceptance of the complaint; if inspection, testing, expert evaluation, or expert review is required, the time needed for such procedures shall not be counted.
If a complainant fabricates facts, forges materials, or obtains evidentiary materials by illegal means to file a complaint, the administrative supervision department shall reject the complaint.

Article 62 When handling a complaint, the administrative supervision department shall have the right to consult and copy relevant documents and materials, and to investigate the relevant circumstances, and the relevant units and individuals shall cooperate. When necessary, the administrative supervision department may order the suspension of the tendering and bidding activities.
Staff members of an administrative supervision department shall keep confidential the State secrets and trade secrets learned during the process of supervision and inspection according to law.

Article 63 If a tenderer commits any of the following acts of restricting or excluding potential bidders, the relevant administrative supervision department shall impose a penalty in accordance with Article 51 of the Tendering and Bidding Law:
(1) For a project that should undergo open tendering according to law, failing to publish a pre-qualification announcement or tender announcement on the designated media in accordance with the provisions;
(2) The contents of the pre-qualification announcement or tender announcement for the same tendering project published on different media are inconsistent, affecting potential bidders' applications for pre-qualification or bidding.
If a tenderer of a project that must undergo tendering according to law fails to publish a pre-qualification announcement or tender announcement in accordance with the provisions, thereby constituting evasion of tendering, a penalty shall be imposed in accordance with Article 49 of the Tendering and Bidding Law.

Article 65 If a tendering agency bids, acts as an agent for bidding, or provides consulting services to bidders in the tendering project for which it acts as an agent, or if an intermediary institution that accepts the entrustment to prepare a base price participates in the bidding of the project for which it prepares the base price, or prepares bid documents or provides consulting services for the bidders of such project, legal liability shall be investigated in accordance with Article 50 of the Tendering and Bidding Law.

Article 66 If a tenderer collects a bid bond or performance bond in excess of the proportions specified in these Regulations, or fails to refund the bid bond and the bank deposit interest for the corresponding period in accordance with the provisions, the relevant administrative supervision department shall order it to make corrections and may impose a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan; if losses are caused to others, compensation liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 69 Any person that transfers or leases qualification or qualification certificates for others to use in bidding shall be subject to administrative penalties in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 70 If a tenderer of a project that must undergo tendering according to law fails to establish a bid evaluation committee in accordance with the provisions, or determines or replaces members of the bid evaluation committee in violation of the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations, the relevant administrative supervision department shall order it to make corrections and may impose a fine of not more than 100,000 yuan, and shall give sanctions to the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible of the unit according to law; the evaluation conclusions made by the illegally determined or replaced members of the bid evaluation committee shall be invalid, and a new evaluation shall be conducted according to law.
If a state functionary illegally interferes in the selection of members of the bid evaluation committee in any manner, legal liability shall be investigated in accordance with Article 80 of these Regulations.

Article 72 If a member of the bid evaluation committee accepts property or other benefits from a bidder, the property accepted shall be confiscated, a fine of not less than 3,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed, the member's qualification as a member of the bid evaluation committee shall be revoked, and the member shall not participate in the bid evaluation of projects that must undergo tendering according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 74 If a winning bidder fails to enter into a contract with the tenderer without justifiable reasons, imposes additional conditions on the tenderer when signing the contract, or fails to submit a performance bond in accordance with the requirements of the tender documents, its qualification for winning the bid shall be revoked and the bid bond shall not be refunded. For a winning bidder of a project that must undergo tendering according to law, the relevant administrative supervision department shall order it to make corrections and may impose a fine of not more than 10‰ of the amount of the winning bid project.

Article 75 If the tenderer and the winning bidder fail to enter into a contract in accordance with the tender documents and the winning bidder's bid document, the main terms of the contract are inconsistent with the contents of the tender documents and the winning bidder's bid document, or the tenderer and the winning bidder conclude an agreement that deviates from the substantive content of the contract, the relevant administrative supervision department shall order them to make corrections and may impose a fine of not less than 5‰ but not more than 10‰ of the amount of the winning bid project.

Article 76 If a winning bidder assigns the project for which the bid was won to others, divides the project into parts and assigns them separately to others, subcontracts part of the main or critical work of the project for which the bid was won in violation of the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations, or if the subcontractor sub-subcontracts the work, the assignment or subcontract shall be invalid, and a fine of not less than 5‰ but not more than 10‰ of the amount of the assigned or subcontracted project shall be imposed; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall also be confiscated; the business may be ordered to suspend operations for rectification; if the circumstances are serious, the administrative authority for industry and commerce shall revoke the business license.

Article 77 If a bidder or any other interested party fabricates facts, forges materials, or obtains evidentiary materials by illegal means to file a complaint, causing losses to others, compensation liability shall be borne according to law.
If a tenderer fails to reply to an objection in accordance with the provisions and continues with the tendering and bidding activities, the relevant administrative supervision department shall order it to make corrections; if it refuses to make corrections or is unable to make corrections and the result of winning the bid is affected, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 81 of these Regulations.

Article 78 The State shall establish a credit system for tendering and bidding. The relevant administrative supervision departments shall, according to law, publicize the administrative handling decisions on illegal acts of parties such as tenderers, tendering agencies, bidders, and members of bid evaluation committees.

Article 79 If a project approval or verification department fails to approve or verify the scope of tendering, the method of tendering, or the organizational form of tendering for a project according to law, sanctions shall be given to the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible of the unit according to law.
If a relevant administrative supervision department fails to perform its duties according to law, fails to investigate and deal with acts that violate the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations according to law, or fails to handle complaints in accordance with the provisions or fails to publicize the administrative handling decisions on illegal acts of parties involved in tendering and bidding according to law, sanctions shall be given to the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible according to law.
If a staff member of a project approval or verification department or a relevant administrative supervision department engages in favoritism, abuses power, or neglects duties, constituting a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 81 If a tendering and bidding activity of a project that must undergo tendering according to law violates the provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law and these Regulations, materially affects the result of winning the bid, and cannot be remedied by corrective measures, the tendering, bidding, and winning of the bid shall be invalid, and a new round of tendering or bid evaluation shall be conducted according to law.

Article 82 The Tendering and Bidding Association shall carry out activities in accordance with its articles of association formulated according to law, and shall strengthen industry self-discipline and services.

Article 83 Where the laws and administrative regulations on government procurement have other provisions on the tendering and bidding of government procurement of goods and services, such provisions shall prevail.
Article 84 These Regulations shall come into force as of February 1, 2012.
